beforeImage.name: Summit Carbon Solutions
beforeImage.description: Summit Carbon Solutions is developing a carbon capture, transportation, and permanent sequestration system for ethanol plants and other industrial facilities in the Midwest. Its end market is the low-carbon fuels and industrial decarbonization value chain, with customers that need lower lifecycle carbon intensity and permanent CO2 storage. The company follows an asset-heavy infrastructure model built around pipeline transportation and geological sequestration rather than a services-only offering. Public disclosures describe a system of about 2,000 miles of pipeline designed to capture up to 20 million tons of carbon dioxide per year across Iowa, Minnesota, Nebraska, South Dakota, and North Dakota. TPG Rise Climate invested $300 million in May 2022 as part of Summit's more than $1 billion equity raise alongside existing sponsors including Tiger Infrastructure Partners Fund III and Continental Resources.

afterImage.name: Summit Carbon Solutions
afterImage.description: Summit Carbon Solutions is developing a carbon-dioxide capture, transportation and permanent-sequestration network for ethanol producers in the Midwest. The company is an active development-stage infrastructure platform, but no construction start, full project-finance close or revised commercial-operation date was identified through August 19, 2026. After a 2026 reroute, the current core is focused on Iowa, Nebraska and Wyoming and retains 27 Iowa ethanol plants while removing approximately 200 route miles; the former approximately 2,000-mile, five-state and 20-million-ton annual design should not be treated as the current approved or operating footprint. Tiger Infrastructure Partners Fund III invested in 2021 and remains the qualifying infrastructure owner. TPG Rise Climate contributed $300 million to the 2022 equity raise through a climate-private-equity strategy and is therefore not counted as a qualifying infrastructure-fund owner. Project, pipeline, capture, storage and site LLCs remain subordinate to the single Summit platform.
